sites.name: Ursel
sites.allied: Mixed RAF and USAAF aircraft; many Spitfires already withdrawn
sites.scope: Later published loss counts of three and six destroyed differ.

sites.name: Volkel
sites.german: JG 6 intended assignment; identity of all aircraft in RAF report open
sites.allied: RAF Regiment 2834, 2809 and 2874 LAA Squadrons; RAF and RNZAF Tempests in later accounts
sites.scope: The RAF ground report describes an attack by more than 20 aircraft. A secondary reconstruction says JG 6 failed to find the field and based aircraft were unharmed. Record approach, ground damage and formation attribution separately.

sites.name: Woensdrecht
sites.allied: No. 132 Wing RAF
sites.scope: Eight aircraft in the RAF gun report. Local history dates No. 322 Squadron's arrival to 1 January, without establishing its participation in the morning engagement.

sites.name: Helmond
sites.allied: RAF Regiment 2873, 2875 and 2881 LAA Squadrons
sites.scope: The RAF report provides timing and gun activity. Air combat and aircraft parked on the field need separate accounting.

sites.name: Étain–Rouvres
sites.allied: 362nd Fighter Group based there; 358th Fighter Group interception en route
sites.scope: Lowe says the Gruppe scattered and Étain escaped attack. The intercepting 367th and 366th Fighter Squadrons were flying from Toul–Croix de Metz.

sites.name: Knokke / Le Zoute
sites.allied: RAF/Allied field in official airfield catalogue
sites.scope: A later target summary mentions a possible mistaken attack. No unit return or independent loss figure is established here.

timeline.text: The Ardennes offensive opened. NIMH dates the intended start of the air operation to 16 December. Bad weather postponed the mass raid.
Another synthesis places the originally envisaged air attack on the day after the ground offensive began.
No. 83 Group airfields, including Eindhoven and Volkel, faced German air attacks. These earlier raids are distinct from Bodenplatte.
The Air Historical Branch records further German attacks on 83 Group airfields.
A German raid hit the Communications Flight dispersal at Eindhoven.
NIMH records that most of the Spitfires at Ursel had already moved to Britain by the day before the attack.
German formations flew low and maintained radio silence. The RAF study describes tactical surprise followed by engagements with anti-aircraft units and increasing Allied fighter opposition.
Pilots from all three squadrons of the 365th Fighter Group were back in the air that afternoon after sharing aircraft and salvaging serviceable machines.
The Ninth Air Force continued ground support, escorts, sweeps and patrols. Its bomber count describes wider theatre operations.
timeline.locator: 1 January, Ninth Air Force tactical operations

timeline.text: The 368th Fighter Group chronology records armed reconnaissance towards Trier, Cochem and Sinzig.
Günter Capito took over I./JG 1 following the death of Georg Hackbarth; Emil Demuth led in the air.
The 368th Fighter Group landed at Metz after armed reconnaissance. The advance echelon had reached the field on New Year's Day.
A Second TAF intelligence summary retained the RAF Regiment's 43 destruction claims. A July Regiment report gave a different account.
No. 350 Squadron's published chronology records its Spitfire strength restored.
I./JG 1 left Twente for the Eastern Front. NIMH describes further losses during the move. These fall outside the 1 January tally.
